blocks.html: Normally, the conditional of an if-statement is evaluated at runtime.
blocks.preview: Normally, the conditional of an if-statement is evaluated at runtime.

blocks.html: However, consider the case where the conditional is a constant expression, such as in the following example:
blocks.preview: However, consider the case where the conditional is a constant expression, such

blocks.html:
#include <iostream>

int main()
{
	constexpr double gravity{ 9.8 };

	// reminder: low-precision floating point literals of the same type can be tested for equality
	if (gravity == 9.8) // constant expression, always true
		std::cout << "Gravity is normal.\n";   // will always be executed
	else
		std::cout << "We are not on Earth.\n"; // will never be executed

	return 0;
}
Because gravity is constexpr and initialized with value 9.8, the conditional gravity == 9.8 must evaluate to true. As a result, the else-statement will never be executed.

blocks.html: C++17 introduces the constexpr if statement, which requires the conditional to be a constant expression. The conditional of a constexpr-if-statement will be evaluated at compile-time.

blocks.html: If the constexpr conditional evaluates to true, the entire if-else will be replaced by the true-statement. If the constexpr conditional evaluates to false, the entire if-else will be replaced by the false-statement (if it exists) or nothing (if there is no else).

blocks.html: To use a constexpr-if-statement, we add the constexpr keyword after the if:
blocks.preview: To use a constexpr-if-statement, we add the constexpr keyword after the if:

blocks.html:
#include <iostream>

int main()
{
	constexpr double gravity{ 9.8 };

	if constexpr (gravity == 9.8) // now using constexpr if
		std::cout << "Gravity is normal.\n";
	else
		std::cout << "We are not on Earth.\n";

	return 0;
}
When the above code is compiled, the compiler will evaluate the conditional at compile time, see that it is always true, and keep only the single statement std::cout << "Gravity is normal.\n";.

Best practice

Favor constexpr if statements over non-constexpr if statements when the conditional is a constant expression.
